subject: Minimal-impact pinning and fallback timetable for private deployment (AcmeRetail)
messages:
From: Claire Ng <claire.ng@acmeretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-oncall@acmeretail.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Planned maintenance for inference cluster w. pin/fallback requests

Hi Jonas,

We're planning a maintenance window for our private Redwood deployment (VPC) to apply the 2.1.4 -> 2.2.0 patch set (security + runtime kernel improvements). Our compliance team requires a brief written plan that covers:

- Version pin approach (how to freeze traffic on known-good 2.1.x during rollout)
- Expected downtime per shard/node and overall SLA exposure
- Rollback triggers and estimated time to revert
- Contact list for immediate escalation

Our preferred window is July 12 02:00-05:00 UTC. Can your ops team confirm feasibility and provide a minimal-impact schedule? We also need the node map and manifest you will use.

Thanks,
Claire
Ops Manager
AcmeRetail

--
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ng <claire.ng@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance for inference cluster w. pin/fallback requests

Claire — thanks for the heads-up. We can support July 12 but I want to propose a timeboxing and low-risk rollout that keeps customer traffic routed to a pinned 2.1.x variant while a canary slice moves to 2.2.0.

High level proposal (draft):
1) Pre-checks and manifest publish — T-48h: node-map + patch-manifest-v2.json shared with oncall.
2) Dry run on staging fleet — T-24h.
3) Window start (02:00 UTC): open canary group (10% of nodes) -> observe 30m telemetry.
4) If green, phase 2: 30% more nodes over 45m with rolling KV drain per host.
5) Hold and stabilize — 30m.
6) If still green, final 60% in two waves, each with automated pin update and health gates.

Rollback triggers we typically use: sustained error rate >1.5% above baseline for 15m, latency P95 > baseline by 200ms for 5m, or failing canary healthchecks. Estimated revert time to full 2.1.x traffic: 20-30 minutes (dependent on KV cache recovery).

I'm looping in Laura for network maintenance windows and Karthik for routing/fallback specifics. I'll put a concise runbook together and attach the proposed window ics + manifest.

Jonas
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

--
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Claire Ng <claire.ng@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance for inference cluster w. pin/fallback requests

Thanks Jonas. Quick notes from a network/ops scheduling perspective:

- The July 12 02:00-05:00 UTC window works for the region, but Acme has a billing cutoff at 04:45 UTC — recommend we finish disruptive steps by 04:30 UTC and move non-disruptive telemetry collection to a post-window slice.
- Canary sizing: 10% is fine; prefer to select canary hosts that are spread across AZs to reduce blast radius. See attached node-map.csv (proposed canary nodes highlighted).
- KV drain: plan for 4–6 minutes of graceful drain per node when we rotate traffic; ensure the drain script is run with --max-inflight 2 to avoid sudden evictions.
- Network maintenance: we'll put a /29 ACL exception for the patch orchestrator during the window and pre-warm the NAT sessions.

Attachments: proposed-window.ics, node-map.csv

Laura
Sr. Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

--
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Ng <claire.ng@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 12:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance for inference cluster w. pin/fallback requests

Echoing the plan — a few specifics on routing and rollback mechanics:

- Traffic pinning: we will use the route table override to pin 100% of traffic to the 2.1.x image while we test canaries. Canary traffic is split via header-based routing using existing weight rules.
- Fallback automation: we’ll deploy a short-lived circuit-breaker Lambda that watches health gates and can trigger route-table rollback; manual confirmation required for cluster-wide rollback.
- Rollback steps (concise):
  1) Halt rollout job (orchestration API -> pause).
  2) Flip route override to 2.1.x (propagation ~30s across control plane).
  3) Run fast-cache-invalidate on canary hosts (script included in patch-manifest-v2.json).
  4) Validate client-level latencies and error counts for 10m window.

Estimated operator time for manual rollback: 10–20 minutes to restore routing + 15–30 minutes for cache warm-up. Biggest risk is stateful KV shards that need rehydration; plan to monitor those closely.

Karthik
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

--
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Claire Ng <claire.ng@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 14:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance for inference cluster w. pin/fallback requests

Thanks all — a couple of notes from release/version stewardship side:

- Pinning strategy: prefer read-only pins (decouple metadata pin from runtime image) so we can continue to receive telemetry from pinned nodes without forcing restarts. If we must change runtime artifacts, perform a staged warm-restart with health-check gating.
- Version shelfing: publish the 2.1.x shelf tag in the control plane before the window so we can flip back instantly.
- Quantization/optimizer risk: 2.2.0 includes a new kernel path that alters int8 behavior for certain transformer layers; include a small regression eval (10 queries per model family) in the canary verification to ensure token-level quality is within thresholds.
- Rollback SLA: because of KV warming, call the rollback 'recover' window; expect potential 10–20% degraded throughput for up to 60 minutes post-rollback for heavy customer traffic patterns.

I'll add these checks to the runbook at the Drive link and attach the patch manifest with the cache invalidation steps.

Soojin
Release Manager
Redwood Inference

--
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ng <claire.ng@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance for inference cluster w. pin/fallback requests

Claire — putting the plan in one place for sign-off. Please reply with OK or any changes by EOD July 6 so we can lock manifests and run rehearsals.

Agreed plan (summary):
- Window: July 12, 02:00-05:00 UTC. Disruptive steps complete by 04:30 UTC.
- Canary: 10% spread across AZs; staging dry-run 24h prior.
- Pinning: route-table override to keep 2.1.x as customer default; canary routed to 2.2.0 by weight rules.
- Rollback triggers: error rate threshold, latency spike, failing regression evals. Manual confirm required for cluster-wide rollback.
- Estimated revert: routing restore 0.5 min; cache and throughput recovery 20–60 minutes depending on KV rehydration.
- Escalation contacts: Jonas Weber (ops lead) + Laura Bennett (network) + Karthik Iyer (SRE) + Soojin Lee (release).

Attachments included: proposed-window.ics, patch-manifest-v2.json, node-map.csv

When you confirm, we'll publish the manifest and run the staging rehearsal on July 11.

Jonas
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
